steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Look here, Holst!

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: You've got to hand it to Clément. He really planted the flowers in front of the statue, prettier than anywhere else.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: I'm surprised Stefano was okay with it, digging a hole in the sacrarium floor, searching for the right dirt, all that.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Take it easy. You're injured.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: It's just a little scratch.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Even little scratches can get worse.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: And call me Gerald.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Alright, alright. You're starting to nag like Stefano.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: That's why his face is all wrinkly. Don't end up like him.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Worry less, meddle less. That's the key to a long life.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't say that. Stefano wants the best for the abbey.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It's thanks to him that we get to live here.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: I know, I'm just saying he worries too much.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: I'm afraid it'll become too much for him.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Stefano is considered stubborn, even amongst the Sankta. He won't budge on what he thinks is right.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But that's one of the reasons we've found refuge here.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: He says the Sarkaz are just like other people.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: And he's right.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Well, you and I, we'll have his back if things become too much for him. We'll repay our debt.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: And stop thinking about what happened in the past. We turned our backs on Theresa when we left Kazdel. We can't go back, Gerald.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Neither of us can.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You don't need to remind me.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I don't remember when I stopped believing in Her Highness's vision... I couldn't see the future of the Sarkaz in our two rulers.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: It's okay.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm fine. We have a new life now.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I led those who wanted to leave away from Kazdel. I'll take responsibility.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Life is much better than it used to be.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Be careful. We don't have the same resources we did before, and there are some tough customers among those bandits.

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Aren't you being a little too careful?

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: How long will it take for the infamous mercenary to become a humble hunter out in the middle of nowhere? Five? Ten? Hahaha!

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: ...Gerald.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Have you really thought about what you'll look like when you put down your weapons for real, and settle in as a humble hunter?

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: What will I look like?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No, I've never thought about it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: What will I look like...?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You'll see for yourself, Eileen.
A long time ago, Gerald used to look up at the night sky when he needed a breather after killing.
The sky is an oppressive black. The campfire has gone out, and even the embers have cooled.
Bloodied mercenaries wipe away the dirt from their faces, gazing at their equally battered comrades, briefly pondering questions they hardly have the luxury to think about.
Can Sarkaz like them truly hope for a happy life?
He once believed that the day would come when the Sarkaz rebuilt their home, but he feels more helpless with each passing day.
They have shed too much blood. They will run out of blood before their monarch's vision comes true.
Eventually, Gerald abandoned Kazdel, bringing along those gasping for breath, running from the land they once fought to the death for.
They hid from the world, ultimately finding a place that would take them. All they wanted was a normal, peaceful life.
The dream came true, once.
When did life turn bitter and oppressive?
It is like a fine dish on the table that no one has tasted.
It has gone bad through no one's doing.
If only blood can end this all...
Then there is only one thing left to do.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't bother trying to change my mind, Clément.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I can't go, and I won't go.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I never told you my old name. It's not a past I'm proud of. An infamous deserter, a broken man.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: With me here, they have an excuse to harm the others.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't be so sad. I'm just going to see Eileen. Death is familiar enough to me, I used to trade in death.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: My life is a small price to pay for the lives of all the others.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: And don't worry about the ones left behind. They'll follow my order.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Raimund is young. He might be impetuous. Do try to calm him down, won't you?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Finally...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Tell Stefano that we probably shouldn't have stopped, back when we were wandering the wastes. Maybe we shouldn't have tried to stay.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But this place was too good.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It was like a dream, living together for so many years. Sooner or later, though, we all have to wake up.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Tell Stefano... gratias, and me paenitet.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'll leave the rest to you, Clément.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Here, at the end of it all...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Am I a hunter, or am I still that mercenary?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm sorry, Eileen. I don't suppose you'd like what I've become, what I look like now.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: ...Dawn has broken.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It seemed like a lot has happened, but then it also seemed like it all happened in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It was a long night, wasn't it?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Nothing worthy of your time, Senior Federico.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I just wanted to find a flower. Gerald shouldn't go to see Eileen empty-handed.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But it looks like the fire last night burned everything. There's nothing left.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If it's just a flower you want, you wouldn't need to come here.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You don't understand, Senior Federico. It's not the same.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The flowers here were different. A special breed grown only in this monastery.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They represent friendship and hope.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes, friendship and hope. The abbot told me they were a symbol of Laterano's partnership with Iberia, one of the abbey's most important possessions.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Beautiful. I was struck, immediately.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: There used to be flowerbeds all over the abbey, covering every inch when you looked down from the bell tower during bloom season.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Eileen loved the sight of it. So did Gerald.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Many were scared to talk to the Sarkaz. But they got along a lot better after the first bloom season.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: People realized that the cruel and warlike Sarkaz would stop to take a look when they passed by the flowerbeds. They would take a flower or two to put in their homes.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: They weren't fearsome desperados. They were no different from us.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There is one here.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Ah, you mean the one beneath the statue.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I saw it. It was lucky to lie beneath the statue when it fell.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But it's not the one I wanted.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Look at it. Don't you see?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It may have hid itself beneath the statue, but its stem is broken, and its petals are burned.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But it's still here.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Is it?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I used to believe there were things that would survive, no matter the adversity. You may laugh, but I truly did.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Life wasn't easy, but all was good.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Amita Nina would make snacks for the kids when she has the time.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Have you ever heard of herb pizzelle?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Amita Nina and Hyman made them from a Lateran recipe using Sarkaz herbs. A dessert that everyone loved, one that belonged to this abbey, and this abbey alone.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Amita Nina used to say that tasting bitter fruit is all well and good, but the children should grow up knowing more than bitterness.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: They should know what sweetness tastes like.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will commit this dessert to memory.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Ha. It's not important. We forgot the taste of sweetness a long time ago.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: No one makes pizzelle anymore.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I find myself curious at times.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: If Sankta weren't so special, if everyone in Laterano was mundane, normal, insignificant as I am...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Would the Holy City still look the same?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Would Laterano be Laterano?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I don't know.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: That's a shame.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you no longer have faith? Have your beliefs changed?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I was just made to see reality.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Things are not as immutable as people think. Testing them only harms them.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: One little flaw, one little imperfection, one tiny, little wound, and it's broken beyond repair.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Like the flower you found.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The flower I'm looking for is no longer here.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It's almost time for Matins. I should go.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Goodbye, Senior Federico.
Federico Giallo stands alone in the morning light of the sacrarium.
The marks left behind by the flames have already been scrubbed away. Deprived of its furnishings, the sacrarium feels empty, with only the sound of footsteps to fill it.
Federico is an outstanding Executor. He has been with the Notarial Hall for six years, carrying out his duties with excellence.
But this is his first year as a saint. There is no one to guide him or instruct him.
The silent saint picks up the broken and burned flower.
The statue protected it from the flames. It was a miracle that it survived the fire.
But this miracle is worthless in the eyes of another.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The flower is still here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But it is not the one he wanted?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Wounds beyond repair...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Would Laterano still be Laterano?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Insufficient data to reach a conclusion.
Executor Federico realizes with a start—
Clément's expression was too calm.
He did not mention Gerald's death, nor the arrangements of the other Sarkaz.
What about himself?
Words without action have no power. That is why he did not say he would find out the truth.
Nor did he say he would fulfill Gerald's last request.
Federico gazes at the broken flower before his eyes.
He has a feeling—
A feeling that, someday, he will find the answer to all his questions in this flower.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Mm—uh—

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Morning, Sara... it's time to wake up...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Mm... mmm... zzz...

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Eren! Wake up, Eren!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Mamma came back yesterday!

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Huh?!

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: She came back? Where is she?

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: It must be her! Look—

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: A new blanket from Mamma? It's a little torn...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: But there are pictures of circles on it! And people with wings! Like what Mamma promised us!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Who cares if it's a little torn? Mamma's clothes are torn too. We have to be good.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: I know, I know.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Let's go and find Senior Federico!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Can we play with Senior Federico today?

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: No, silly, we're going to tell Senior Federico that Mamma came back to see us last night, so he doesn't need to worry!
